newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU SEES FINNISH 1997 BUDGET DEFICIT BELOW 3 PCT.
newsitem.headline: EU SEES FINNISH 1997 BUDGET DEFICIT BELOW 3 PCT.

text.p: European Union Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy, reacting to an upward revision of Finland's 1996 budget deficit, predicted that the 1997 figure would still be inside the target set by the Maastricht Treaty for economic and monetary union.
"In 1997, the Finnish public deficit should be below three percent (of gross domestic production)," he said.
De Silguy issued a brief statement after Finland on Monday had revised its deficit for last year to 3.1 percent of GDP from a previous estimate of 2.6 percent.
He said Finland was undertaking "remarkable efforts" to meet the convergence criteria, noting that the deficit had been as high as eight percent of GDP in 1993.
"Even with an upward revision of the 1996 figure, the reduction of the public deficit has reached around five percentage points of GDP between 1993 and 1996," he said.
"All this shows that Finland is making significant and credible progress."
De Silguy said the Commission as usual would assess the budget situation of all EU member states in September. This examination would also include figures for 1996.
For Finland, as for the other countries, a high level of durable convergence was necessary for joining economic and monetary union, he said.
The Commission would take its position on this in March 1998 based on final figures for 1997, on budgets already adopted for 1998 and on future forecasts.
On Tuesday, the Finnish finance ministry stressed that the 1997 public sector deficit would be inside the three-percent limit goal for EMU despite the 1996 overshoot.

State secretary Raimo Sailas told Reuters in Helsinki that even in a worst-case scenario, the 1997 deficit would be safely within the EMU limit. He attributed the revision of the 1996 deficit mainly to non-recurring factors.
